Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 32, verse 3:

(p-183)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah As-Sajdah

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, that they may be guided.﴾ We have already explained this in Surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [Al-Isra': 15].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 32, verse 5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years by your reckoning﴾ (5).

In this noble verse, may He be exalted and majestic, He mentions that He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth, and that it ascends to Him in a day whose extent is a thousand years.

He, exalted, alluded to this meaning in His saying: ﴿Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them. The command descends among them﴾ [at-Talaq: 12]. He has explained in Surah "al-Hajj" that a day with Him, exalted is He, is like a thousand years of what people count, and that is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ [al-Hajj: 47]. And He, exalted is He, said in Surah "Sa'ala sa'il": ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a day the extent of which is fifty thousand years﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 4].

We have mentioned in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" the reconciliation of these verses in two ways:

The first: what Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted through the chain of Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the day of the thousand years in Surah "al-Hajj" is one of the six days in which Allah created the heavens and the earth; the day of the thousand years in Surah "as-Sajdah" is the measure of the travel of the command and its ascent to Him, exalted is He; and the day of fifty thousand years is the Day of Resurrection.

(p-184) The second way: that the intended meaning of all of them is the Day of Resurrection, and that the difference is due to the condition of the believer and the disbeliever. This view is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So that Day will be a difficult day, for the disbelievers, not easy﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 9-10], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day"﴾ [al-Qamar: 8].

We have clarified this second way in Surah "al-Furqan", in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will be better in their resting place and finer in their resting at midday﴾ [al-Furqan: 24]. We have also mentioned in "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" that Abu 'Ubaydah narrated from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah that he was present when Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib were both asked about these verses, and he did not know what to say about them, and he said: "I do not know."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 32, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: The angel of death who has been charged with you will take you back﴾.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that the one who seizes the souls of people is a single, specific angel, and this is the well-known view. In some reports it has come that his name is Izra'il (ʿIzrāʾīl).

Allah has explained in other verses that people are taken back by angels, not by a single angel:

• such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾ [an-Nisa: 97],

• and His saying: ﴿So how will it be when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?﴾ [Muhammad: 27],

• and His saying: ﴿If you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming throes of death while the angels extend their hands﴾ [al-An'am: 93],

• and His saying: ﴿until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him in death, and they do not fail﴾ [al-An'am: 61],

along with other verses.

The clarification of this according to the people of knowledge ('ahl al-ʿilm) is that the one entrusted with seizing souls is a single angel, who is the one mentioned here, but he has assistants who act on his command, drawing out the soul to the throat (ḥulqūm), and then the Angel of Death takes it, or they assist him in other ways.

It has come in the well-known long hadith of al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib that the Prophet ﷺ mentioned in it: "When the Angel of Death takes the soul of the dead person, angels take it swiftly from his hand and ascend with it to the heaven." In it the Prophet ﷺ also explained how the soul of the believer and the soul of the disbeliever are treated after the angels have taken it from the Angel of Death, at the moment he takes it from the body. The hadith of al-Bara' mentioned is authenticated by more than one scholar, and Ibn al-Qayyim in the book "al-Ruh" demonstrated the invalidity of Ibn Hazm's weakening of it.

The summary: the hadith of al-Bara' mentioned indicates that with the Angel of Death there are other angels who take the soul from his hand when he takes it from the body of the dead. As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾ [az-Zumar: 42], there is no difficulty in it, because the angels cannot take anyone's soul except by His will, may He be majestic and exalted: ﴿And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of Allah, a decree with a specified term﴾ [Al 'Imran: 145].

Thus it is established that the attribution of taking back to the Angel of Death in His saying here: ﴿Say: The angel of death who has been charged with you will take you back﴾ [as-Sajdah: 11] is because he is the one commanded to seize souls; and its attribution to the angels in His saying: ﴿So how will it be when the angels take them back﴾ [Muhammad: 27] and similar verses is because the Angel of Death has assistants who act on his command; and its attribution to Allah in His saying: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾ [az-Zumar: 42] is because everything, whatever it may be, occurs only by the decree and destiny of Allah. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah as-Sajdah

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: The angel of death who has been charged with you will take you back﴾ and the rest of the verse.

In this noble verse He attributed taking back to a single angel, and in other verses He attributed it to the group of angels, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take back﴾ [al-Anfal: 50] and His saying: ﴿If you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming throes of death while the angels extend their hands﴾ [al-An'am: 93].

And in another verse He attributed it to Himself, may He be majestic and exalted, namely His saying: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾ [az-Zumar: 42].

The answer to this is clear: its attribution to Himself is because the Angel of Death cannot take the soul of anyone except by His permission and will, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of Allah, a decree with a specified term﴾ [Al 'Imran: 145]. Its attribution to the Angel of Death is because he is the one commanded to seize souls, and its attribution to the angels is because the Angel of Death has angelic assistants under his authority, who act on his command and draw out the soul to the throat, and then the Angel of Death takes it. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 32, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, saying: "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so send us back; we will act righteously. Indeed, we are now certain."﴾ (12).

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "al-A'raf," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the day its interpretation (ta'wil) comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth. So do we have any intercessors?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 53], and in Surah "Maryam," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How clearly they will hear and see on the day they come to Us!﴾ [Maryam: 38].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 32, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."﴾ (13).

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Yunus," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them entirely﴾ [Yunus: 99].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 32, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, then turns away from them? Indeed, We will take retribution against the criminals.﴾ (32:22).

We have already presented the verses that clarify this, together with the explanation of the evil consequences that arise from turning away from the reminder of Allah's verses, in surah "al-Kahf" (the Cave), in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: (p-186) ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord but turns away from them and forgets what his hands have put forward?﴾ [al-Kahf: 57].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 32, verse 26:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whom they walk through their dwellings?﴾

We have already presented some of the verses that clarify this in the end of Surah Maryam, in the discussion of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And how many generations We destroyed before them. Do you perceive any one of them, or hear from them any whisper?﴾ [Maryam: 98].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 32, verse 27:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do they not see that We drive the water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which eat their livestock and themselves? Will they not then see?﴾ (32:27).

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Ta-Ha," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who has made for you the earth as a cradle, and threaded for you therein roads, and sent down from the sky water, and We brought forth thereby pairs of various plants. Eat and graze your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for people of intellect﴾ (20:53-54). We have also explained the meaning of "al-ard al-juruz" (the barren land), together with some Arabic evidence, in Surah "al-Kahf," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it a bare, barren ground﴾ (18:8).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 32, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they say, "When is this victory, if you are truthful?"﴾ (28) ﴿Say, "On the day of victory, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved."﴾ (29).

The most apparent of the opinions of the people of knowledge, in my view, is that the "fath" (victory/opening) in this noble verse is judgment and decision. We have already mentioned that the fattah (one who opens) means the judge, which is an ancient Himyarite dialect, and al-fataha (judgment and decision) is from it. From this is the saying of the poet:

Is there no one to convey to ʿAmr, a messenger, that I am independent of your judgeship (fataha)?

Verses have also come indicating that al-fath means judgment, such as His saying, may He be exalted, concerning His prophet Shuʿayb: ﴿Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, decide (iftah) between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of deciders (al-fatihin)﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 89], meaning: judge between us in truth, and You are the best of judges.

• And His saying, may He be exalted, concerning His prophet Nuh: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me. So decide (iftah) between me and them a decision (fath)"﴾ [al-Shuʿara': 117–118], meaning: judge between me and them a judgment,

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "Our Lord will gather us together; then He will judge (yaftahu) between us in truth, and He is the Knowing Judge (al-Fattah al-ʿAlim)"﴾ [Saba': 26],

• And His saying, may He be exalted: (p-187) ﴿If you seek a decision, the decision has certainly come to you﴾ [al-Anfal: 19],

meaning: if you seek judgment by the destruction of the wrongdoer among you and the Prophet ﷺ, then the decision has come to you, that is, the judgment of the destruction of the wrongdoer, which was their destruction on the day of Badr, as said by more than one scholar. They mentioned that when they intended to go out to Badr, Abu Jahl came, clung to the curtains of the Kaaba, and said: "O Allah, we are the custodians of Your House, we give drink to the pilgrims, and we do such-and-such, and Muhammad has severed the ties of kinship, divided the community, reviled the religion, insulted the gods, and mocked the wisdom of our forefathers. O Allah, destroy the wrongdoer among us and him." Thus he sought judgment against the wrongdoer, and the judgment against the wrongdoer came to them, and they were slain at Badr and went to eternal abiding in the Fire, along with other verses.

According to the view of those among the people of knowledge who say that what is meant by "fath" in the verse is the judgment and decision between them on the Day of Resurrection, there is no difficulty in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "On the day of victory, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them"﴾. And according to the view that what is meant by "fath" in the verse is the judgment between them in this world by the destruction of the disbelievers, as occurred on the day of Badr, the apparent meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "On the day of victory, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them"﴾ is: when they witness death and see the killing. The evidence is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We have believed in Allah alone and disbelieved in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ ﴿But their faith was not going to benefit them when they saw Our might. [That is] the established way of Allah which has already passed among His servants. And the disbelievers were lost therein﴾ [Ghafir: 84–85],

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have now repented"﴾ [al-Nisa': 18],

• And His saying, may He be exalted, concerning Pharaoh: ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims."﴾ ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ [Yunus: 90–91].

And it is not hidden that the saying of those among the people of knowledge that the "fath" in this verse is the conquest of Makkah is incorrect, by the evidence of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say, "On the day of victory, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them"﴾, and it is well known that the conquest of Makkah does not prevent a believer at that time from benefiting from his faith, as is not hidden.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 32, verse 30:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿So wait, [Prophet], and indeed they are waiting.﴾ Its meaning has been made clear in other verses, such as His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Or do they say, "A poet, we await for him the vicissitudes of time"? Say, "Wait, for I am with you among those who wait."﴾ [At-Tur: 30–31]. It is well known that tarabbus (waiting, watching for an outcome) is the same as intizar (waiting). And His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Wait, indeed we are waiting."﴾ [Al-An'am: 158], and other verses besides these.
